title: Design job-state reconstruction and structured retros over the record
summary: The 2026-10-13 addendum (BRIEF.md:488-492) asks that Athena can rebuild any job's state at any point from git and the records, and run structured retros on finished jobs to learn which questions should have been asked of the user earlier. Nothing is built yet (no "reconstruct" or "retro" code in crates/). Under the "designed" default, I read this as one written design doc, with alternatives, that the maintainer can review before any build. It extends roadmap RM-1.

defaults_applied.how: Deliver a written design with alternatives instead of code.
The design cites BRIEF.md lines and existing files for every claim, and labels numbers as estimates.
Written for an outside reader, linked from the roadmap.
One design doc plus the log entries; no code.
The design considers existing tools (git log/worktree, existing crates) before proposing a new one.
The design names which checks would be enforced by test and which stay prose-only.
Criteria require a worked example of reconstruction and retro output, not just a file existing.
The retro design targets the cause of late questions (missing defaults), not individual corrections.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: the maintainer (and a later builder) can judge a concrete plan for two features: as-of reconstruction of a job's state, and a structured retro that outputs candidate questions and defaults.
Audience: the repository owner reviewing designs before build, per the 'designed' default.
Scope is the design, not the implementation; the build is a follow-up job once the design is reviewed.

Inputs are what exists in the repo: job records, git history, the status view (athena status), the decisions log, and the socratic-review and defaults-loop designs. Retro output feeds the defaults loop and the Socratic question generator rather than creating a parallel mechanism.
Reconstruction should work from git and records alone, with stated assumptions about what is absent, since records/ may be missing in a given copy.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new design doc under docs/design/ cites BRIEF.md:488-492 and states the goal and audience: reconstruct a job's state at a point in time, and run retros that find what should have been asked earlier.
The doc defines reconstruction concretely: which inputs (git commits, job records, status view), what the state at a point contains, what is lost when records/ is absent, and the assumptions made.

The doc defines the retro: its steps, its output record shape (the question or default that should have been asked, with evidence from the job's sessions), and how it feeds the defaults loop and the Socratic generator rather than duplicating them.
The doc includes at least two alternatives for each feature with reasons for the choice, and one worked example drawn from a real finished job in this repo, checkable against git history.
The doc says which checks would be enforced by mechanism and which stay prose-only, and gives a staged build plan with a done-when for each stage.
docs/design/roadmap.md RM-1 links to the new doc, and docs/decisions.md and CHANGELOG.md each get an entry with provenance pointing to the 2026-10-13 addendum.
Run `cargo test` and `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check`: all still pass, because any doc-consistency tests that scan docs/ (for example for link or provenance rules) accept the new files.

out_of_scope: Implementing the reconstruct command or retro runner in crates/.
Changing athena.toml, defaults.toml, or workflow files.
Editing BRIEF.md, records/, or other owner files.
Running retros over real jobs and adopting new defaults from them.
departures: Reading accepted is lowered from the reference (0.80) because the request could mean an implementation, and I read it as design-first under the 'designed' default. Other forecasts stay near the reference.
